move.instructions: reviewer_comment is about tests. Which problem does it raise or which improvement does it ask for? Pick the one that fits best.

criteria.missing_case: Names a specific case the tests do not cover: an input, boundary, error path, variant, configuration, platform or interaction
criteria.needs_test: Asks for a test (often a regression test) for the change without naming particular cases
criteria.not_discriminating: The test would pass without the change, does not reach the new code path, or does not test what it claims to
criteria.weak_assertion: An assertion is missing or too loose: it checks only that nothing crashed, a status, a count or a truthy value, and should check the exact result, error, message or side effect
criteria.wrong_expectation: The expected value is wrong, was copied from the current (buggy) output, or the test checks the code against itself
criteria.overspecified: The test pins down incidental details (exact wording, ordering, internal calls, timing, a whole snapshot) and will break on harmless changes
criteria.flaky: The result can vary from run to run: timing, sleeps, ordering, concurrency, randomness, network, clock or machine load
criteria.isolation_cleanup: Shared or global state, leaked resources, temporary files or settings not restored, or tests that depend on each other's order
criteria.environment_assumption: The test assumes something about the machine: platform, architecture, locale, filesystem, permissions, installed tools, build configuration; or its skip conditions are wrong
criteria.test_logic_bug: The test code itself is broken: wrong variable, a loop or branch that never runs, an unawaited call, wrong setup, a check that can never fail
criteria.unrealistic_setup: The test sets up a state or input that cannot happen in practice, or bypasses the real path users take
criteria.mocking: Mocks, stubs or fakes are misused: they hide the behaviour under test, mirror the implementation, or a real object or existing fake should be used
criteria.implementation_coupling: The test reaches into internals or private details instead of testing behaviour through the public interface, or tests at the wrong level (unit versus integration or end to end)
criteria.duplicate_or_parametrize: Tests repeat each other or an existing test, and should be merged, table-driven or parametrised
criteria.reuse_test_infra: An existing test helper, fixture, harness, assertion utility or framework feature should be used
criteria.simplify_reduce: The test is larger or more complex than needed: reduce the reproducer, drop irrelevant setup, remove logic from the test
criteria.placement_naming: The test is in the wrong file, suite or directory, or its name does not say what it tests
criteria.diagnostics: When the test fails it should say why: assertion messages, comparing values instead of booleans, useful output
criteria.explain_test: Asks for a comment or description explaining what the test checks or why
criteria.cost: The test is too slow, heavy or wasteful: iterations, sleeps, timeouts, resources
criteria.different_technique: Proposes another kind of test: fuzzing, property-based, differential, golden or FileCheck output, benchmark, end-to-end
criteria.weakened_or_removed: Tests or assertions were deleted, skipped, disabled or loosened, or expected results were changed, to make the change pass
